question.text: Harini Infrastructure Fund's documents include an indemnification cap of INR 10 crore and a survival period of 3 years from the fund's final closing. What does the survival period signify?

answer.text: Indemnification claims must be brought within 3 years of the final closing; claims raised after this period are time-barred
The fund must survive and continue operations for at least 3 years
The fund manager's employment contract lasts for 3 years
Investors must hold their units for at least 3 years before making any claims

explanation.text: The Logic: In PE/M&A practice, the "survival period" is the contractually agreed window within which an indemnified party must bring its claim. After this period (here, 3 years from the final closing), claims are time-barred regardless of when the underlying loss is discovered. It is not about fund tenure, manager employment, or investor holding requirements. The Trap: The fund-operations option conflates fund tenure with the indemnification survival period — they are different concepts. Note: The XIX-A workbook does not define "indemnification cap," "survival period," or "time-barred claims" as named mechanisms; this is general PE/M&A documentation practice applicable when reading AIF investment agreements.
